The Compiled Form of a Stopping Rule

Source: R/criterion.R
criterion_spec.Rd

Returns a description of a stopping rule as nested lists, from which the compiled descent loop builds the same rule in C++, or NULL where the rule or one of its members has no compiled form.

Usage

criterion_spec(criterion)

Arguments

criterion

A criterion() object.

Value

A list, or NULL.

Details

The rules with a compiled form are those built by crit_grad(), crit_abs_obj(), crit_rel_obj(), crit_abs_par(), crit_rel_par(), crit_never(), crit_any() and crit_all(). The class is read exactly, so that a subclass with a method of its own for crit_met() is evaluated in R. Each element of the result has type ("grad", "abs_obj", "rel_obj", "abs_par", "rel_par", "never", "any" or "all"), and tol, norm or criteria where the rule has them. The compiled rules compute the same quantities as the methods of crit_met(), with the same arithmetic, and combine missing values as any() and all() do. The descent methods (newton(), bfgs(), lbfgs(), gd(), cg(), bb(), chebyshev()) ask the compiled form where one exists; options(optimizers7.compiled_rules = FALSE) makes them ask crit_met() in R instead. Another package that runs the descent loop through the headers in inst/include/optimizers7 passes this list to make_compiled_rule() in rules.h.

See also

crit_met(), crit_any()

Examples

str(criterion_spec(crit_any(crit_grad(), crit_abs_obj(1e-8))))
#> List of 2
#>  $ type    : chr "any"
#>  $ criteria:List of 2
#>   ..$ :List of 3
#>   .. ..$ type: chr "grad"
#>   .. ..$ tol : num 1e-06
#>   .. ..$ norm: chr "max"
#>   ..$ :List of 2
#>   .. ..$ type: chr "abs_obj"
#>   .. ..$ tol : num 1e-08

Tiny <- S7::new_class("Tiny", parent = criterion,
                      properties = list(tol = S7::class_numeric))
S7::method(crit_met, Tiny) <- function(criterion, state)
  abs(state$f_new) < criterion@tol
#> Overwriting method crit_met(<Tiny>)
criterion_spec(Tiny(label = "tiny", tol = 1e-3))
#> NULL
